#!/bin/bash -l
# Flux batch script converted from PBS

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# PBS resources:
#   -l nodes=3:ppn=128
#   -l mem=64gb
#   -l walltime=1:00:00
#   -r n
#   -j oe
#   -q starq

# Request 3 nodes. The original launch used -n 192 ranks.
#flux: -N 3
#flux: -n 192
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=1h

# Omitted PBS option: -l mem=64gb
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted PBS option: -q starq (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted PBS option: -j oe (join stdout/stderr)
# Flux commonly manages stdout/stderr separately; a portable join directive is not guaranteed.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but logs may be split.

# Omitted PBS option: -r n (non-rerunnable)
# Flux does not have a universal portable directive for PBS rerunnable semantics.
# Performance implication: none for performance, but restart behavior/policies may differ.

cd /fs/lustre/cita/zack/jl/dev/LagrangianPerturbationTheory/projectamd
module load openmpi

julia --project -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'
julia --project -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.precompile()'

# PBS used mpiexecjl -n 192; under Flux, use flux-run to launch ranks.
flux run -n 192 -c 1 /fs/lustre/cita/zack/jl/bin/mpiexecjl --project -n 192 julia fft_filter_6144.jl

reasons: PBS requested 64GB of memory (`-l mem=64gb`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.

PBS specified a queue (`-q starq`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
